transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-10
Time: 16:00 - 16:48 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Rivera (Redwood SE), Jasmin Li (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connor (CTO), Priya Desai (Head of Security), Marcus Hill (Engineering Manager), Ana Ruiz (SRE)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on security posture: SOC2/ISO status, SSO/SAML and SSO integrations, RBAC, audit logs, encryption and KMS options, data retention. Customer leaning toward private deployment or Dedicated in VPC for PHI-sensitive workloads; wants attestation docs and network diagrams. Decided next steps and owners.

Topics:
- Compliance baseline (SOC2, ISO)
- Authentication (SSO/SAML, SCIM, IdP)
- Encryption (at-rest and in-transit), KMS integrations
- RBAC and audit logging granularity
- Data retention and deletion policies
- Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: All right everybody hi thanks for joining, we'll do a quick intros then jump into the security posture. I'm Maya from Redwood, with Ethan our SE and Jasmin on CSM.
[00:08] Liam O'Connor: Hey thanks, Liam here CTO at Peridot. Priya is our head of security and Marcus is eng leads and Ana on SRE.
[00:14] Maya Chen: Great, appreciate the time. The plan is to run through SOC2/ISO, auth, encryption, audit logs, and retention, and then map that to hosted vs dedicated vs private. Any other items?
[00:25] Priya Desai: Not from me, that's the hit list. We are particularly sensitive to data residency and key management for some of our ML inference.
[00:32] Ethan Rivera: Totally, we'll focus there. Quick housekeeping — apologies if transcription glitches, we sometimes see "K Vcash" in these notes, that's KV cache not KVcash.
[00:40] Marcus Hill: Ha noted.

[00:45] Maya Chen: First question — compliance state: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attested, we have the reports and we can share the redacted reports and the control matrix. Ethan, any nuance to add?
[00:55] Ethan Rivera: Yep, we also maintain third-party penetration test summaries and a scope doc that shows hosted vs dedicated differences. For Dedicated/Private customers we expose more telemetry and can support tighter controls.
[01:05] Priya Desai: When you say "expose more telemetry" do you mean we get access to raw audit logs or are these pushed to our SIEM?
[01:12] Jasmin Li: We can stream audit logs to customer S3 or push to SIEM via secure syslog/SSE — customers typically pick one. We'll include the event schema.
[01:21] Ana Ruiz: What events are included — user auth, API calls, model loads, KV cache hits?
[01:26] Ethan Rivera: Good question. Our audit logs include API auth events, token operations, model version deploys, deploy rollbacks, and administrative actions. KV cache access at the request-level is in metrics, full per-token traces are not retained by default — there are policies for that.

[01:40] Liam O'Connor: Also want to understand SSO. We use Okta and Azure AD. We need SAML/SCIM provisioning and role mappings into RBAC.
[01:48] Maya Chen: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; role mappings can be configured to map IdP groups to Redwood roles. Ethan, maybe show the RBAC model quickly?
[01:56] Ethan Rivera: Sure. At a high level we have org->project->route scopes. Roles: admin, developer, observer, billing. For Dedicated or Private you can add custom role tags and tighter separation via network and KMS keys.
[02:12] Priya Desai: For our auditors we need proof of SSO enforcement and that service accounts can't bypass SAML. How does Redwood handle service keys?
[02:19] Ethan Rivera: Service tokens exist, yes. They can be scoped per-route and tied to VPCs. For Private we can require all service tokens to be rotated via your KMS/HSM. We also support short-lived tokens with automatic rotation.
[02:32] Marcus Hill: Does Redwood support Bring-Your-Own-KMS? We use AWS KMS for some keys and are evaluating HashiCorp Vault for others.
[02:39] Maya Chen: Yes, BYOK is supported for Private deployments and Dedicated in your VPC. For hosted we have our managed KMS but we also offer KMSe integration patterns like envelope encryption with customer CMKs for sensitive data.
[02:51] Priya Desai: Envelope encryption? Can you clarify — the model artifacts and request data encrypted under our CMK or Redwood's?
[02:59] Ethan Rivera: For hosted, by default Redwood encrypts at rest with our KMS, but for customers who need more control we can do envelope encryption where the data key is wrapped with your CMK so ultimately your CMK controls key usage. For Private, everything can be configured to use your KMS/HSM.

[03:20] Ana Ruiz: Network-wise, for Private we need the deployment inside our VPC with private subnets and no public egress for inference requests. Is that standard?
[03:28] Ethan Rivera: Yes, Private deployments can be fully air-gapped. For Dedicated we typically run in your cloud account via a dedicated account or tenancy and we can peer or use private links. We'll provide a network diagram.
[03:39] Liam O'Connor: That diagram would be great — show where audit logs flow, how secrets are stored, and the control plane boundary.
[03:45] Maya Chen: We'll include that.

[03:50] Priya Desai: Data retention — we have legal needs to keep transcripts for 7 years for some customers but delete raw PII after 90 days. How does Redwood manage per-route retention?
[03:59] Jasmin Li: You can set per-route retention windows in the console; default retention for hosted logs is 30 days but for Dedicated/Private we can set retention policies and automatic purging. We also support redaction at ingestion for PII tokens and can run a scrub pipeline.
[04:15] Marcus Hill: Is there an API to purge data programmatically if we get a DSAR or a legal hold?
[04:20] Ethan Rivera: Yes, there is a purge API and an export API. For Private deployments purge operations can be run locally and audited. We log the purge action in the audit trail.

[04:30] Priya Desai: Auditing — we need immutable audit trails and tamper evidence. Does Redwood use append-only logs or sign logs?
[04:36] Ethan Rivera: Our hosted audit logs are WORM-like with retention policies and we provide cryptographic checksums for export. For Private you can integrate with your own WORM store and we support signing via KMS so you can provide tamper evidence.

[04:50] Liam O'Connor: Ok, what about model reuse and cache — we're concerned about leakage across customers. Is there multitenancy isolation at the KV cache level?
[04:59] Ethan Rivera: Isolation is enforced per-tenant. KV cache is namespaced per-tenant and cannot be accessed across tenants. For Dedicated and Private, caches run in your tenancy and are fully isolated.
[05:10] Priya Desai: Are there any residual artifacts after model inference? Temp files, disk caches?
[05:15] Ethan Rivera: We clear ephemeral artifacts when jobs complete; persistent artifacts are only the ones you choose to persist (models, datasets). For hosted we have policies; we can provide a list of filesystem paths and retention semantics.

[05:30] Maya Chen: Let's talk SLOs and incident response — do you have a preferred runbook for notifying customers of a potential data incident?
[05:36] Priya Desai: We expect 24-hour initial notification and a detailed incident report within 72 hours for any data exposure.
[05:42] Jasmin Li: Redwood's SLA and incident response docs support that — we can do the 24-hour notification for any customer-impacting security incident and provide a postmortem. For Dedicated we also offer a dedicated channel.

[05:55] Marcus Hill: One more question on encryption in transit — do you terminate TLS at our edge or at Redwood?
[06:01] Ethan Rivera: For Private and Dedicated in your VPC you can terminate TLS on your side or on Redwood's side within the private link; mutual TLS options are available for stronger identity.

[06:12] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good; what are blocker items for us to choose Private vs Dedicated vs hosted? Cost is a factor but security requirements may push to Private.
[06:20] Maya Chen: Right — quick heuristics: hosted is fastest/cheapest but with Redwood-managed KMS and shared control plane; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity in your cloud account and stronger isolation; Private gives you full control of the control plane and networking. For PHI and strict compliance we often see customers choose Private.

[06:37] Priya Desai: We'll likely pilot Dedicated in our account and, if tick boxes pass, move to Private.

[06:42] Maya Chen: Great. Next steps recap — we'll send the SOC2/ISO docs and the network diagram, Ethan will prepare the VPC/Private deployment checklist, and Priya will share data retention requirements. Jasmin will set up the technical deep-dive scheduling.
[06:56] Liam O'Connor: Perfect. Anything else?
[07:00] Ana Ruiz: No, thanks everyone.

[07:02] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and a proposed time for the deep dive.

[07:07] (call ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings — e.g., "K-M-S" appeared as "K M S" and "KV cache" as "KV cash" — cleaned inline where obvious but original recording had slurred acronyms.

References shared during call:
- Redwood SOC 2 summary (link to be emailed)

End of transcript.
